option_relations.rationale: The option describes acute coronary syndrome, which is ruled out by coronary angiography showing nonobstructive disease and unchanged troponin. The leaf describes cardiac tamponade due to metastatic lung cancer, which is a different diagnosis.

ST-segment elevation is a finding/manifestation, and myocardial metastasis from lung cancer is part of the etiology leading to the overall condition described in the leaf. The leaf 'Cardiac tamponade due to malignant pericardial effusion from metastatic lung cancer with myocardial metastasis' encompasses the underlying cause and a major complication.

The option 'Cardiac metastasis from lung cancer (intracardiac mass)' is a component of the more comprehensive diagnosis described in the leaf 'Cardiac tamponade due to malignant pericardial effusion from metastatic lung cancer with myocardial metastasis'. The leaf includes the metastasis and its complication (tamponade).

The option 'Metastatic cardiac tumor (secondary to lung cancer)' is a component of the more comprehensive diagnosis described in the leaf 'Cardiac tamponade due to malignant pericardial effusion from metastatic lung cancer with myocardial metastasis'. The leaf includes the metastatic tumor and its complication (tamponade).
